gaps.sentence: We had ___ luggage that the taxi couldn't take it all.
gaps.explanation: 'So much luggage that …' — luggage is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with excuses; deliver on time or do not bother coming.
gaps.explanation: 'Has no patience with' — 'no' directly negates the noun.

gaps.sentence: If you walk instead of driving, you'll spend ___ on petrol.
gaps.explanation: 'Spend less' is the comparative with uncountable money; 'fewer' is for countable nouns.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two proposals has been approved so far.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' — 'none' is for three or more.

gaps.sentence: Very ___ applicants had the required experience.
gaps.hint: 'very' + negative quantifier with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Very few' means almost none and is used with countables; 'very a few' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: ___ lakes in this region freeze in winter.
gaps.explanation: 'Most lakes' speaks about lakes in general; 'most of' would need 'the lakes'.

gaps.sentence: There are ___ than forty applicants for every training place.
gaps.explanation: 'More than' + number expresses quantities above a figure.

gaps.sentence: I looked everywhere, but I couldn't find my keys ___.
gaps.explanation: After a negative verb, 'anywhere' is used; 'somewhere' belongs to affirmative sentences.
